method: Work on the WGS84 ellipsoid with a = 6,378,137 m and f = 1/298.257223563. A UTM zone's central meridian is 6z - 183 degrees, and the longitude difference from it is wrapped to -180..180 degrees. Grid convergence is evaluated with the transverse Mercator series through the third power of the longitude difference, gamma = delta sin(phi) + (delta^3 / 3) sin(phi) cos^2(phi) (1 + 3 eta^2), where phi is the geodetic latitude and eta^2 = e'^2 cos^2(phi) uses the second eccentricity squared; delta is in radians and the result is converted to degrees. A positive value means grid north lies east of true north, so true azimuth = grid azimuth + gamma and grid azimuth = true azimuth - gamma, each normalised to 0..360 with 360 treated as due north. Convergence is zero on the central meridian and at the equator and grows with latitude and with the distance from the central meridian. A longitude more than 6 degrees from the chosen zone's central meridian is refused and the refusal names the zone that contains it, because the series is only accurate to about 0.01 arc seconds within 3 degrees and 0.1 arc seconds out to 6 degrees. Latitude is accepted from -80 to 84 degrees (the UTM band), longitude from -180 to 180, the zone from 1 to 60 with a blank zone derived from the longitude, and the bearing from 0 to 360 degrees. Decimal commas are accepted; blank, non-numeric, exponent-notation and out-of-range values are refused with the failing field named. Magnetic declination, local attraction, projection scale factor, geoid height and grid-to-ground distance reduction are not modelled.
